explanation: Removing your shoes before entering a Turkish home is standard practice and a sign of respect and cleanliness — hosts often provide slippers. Mosques also require all visitors to remove their shoes at the entrance, where shelves or bags are typically provided.
local_tip: Take your shoes off at the door without being asked, and do the same before entering any mosque.

also_check.note: Removing shoes is mandatory, usually at a genkan entryway, with slippers provided for indoor use.
Shoe removal isn't universal; it depends on the household, so it's best to follow the host's lead.
Shoes are removed before entering homes and many temples as a sign of respect and cleanliness.

sources.title: Mosque manners — Customs and etiquette in Turkey
